Title: MACC rubbishes report senior Umno leader to be called up after assembly
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission has rubbished reports that a senior Umno leader is expected to be called up for questioning after the party's general assembly.
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said there was no such individual on the commission's radar.
"As far as I'm concerned, and as far as MACC is concerned, there is none.
"I don't understand where this report came from or how it emerged. There is no such person on our list," he told reporters today.
MORE TO COME
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Former company GM on remand for alleged power abuse
Article:
SHAH ALAM: A former general manager of a real estate investment holding company is on remand for two days until tomorrow on suspicion of abusing his position to secure benefits and rewards.
Magistrate Wan Noora Nisa Ngadirin issued the remand order against the man, who is in his 30s, following an application by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) at the Shah Alam magistrate's court here.
According to a source, the suspect was arrested at about 2pm yesterday at the Selangor MACC office.
"Preliminary investigations revealed that the suspect allegedly committed the offence between 2023 and 2025 when he was the general manager of the company.
"The suspect is believed to have abused his power and position regarding promotions, salary adjustments, and the awarding of bonuses in a manner that did not comply with established standard operating procedures (SOPs)," the source said.
Meanwhile, Selangor MACC Director Mohd Azwan Ramli confirmed the arrest when contacted and said that the case is being investigated under Section 23 of the MACC Act 2009.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: '33-vote support for senator candidate shows Perak unity government remains strong'
Article:
IPOH: The unanimous 33-vote support among state government representatives for Perak PKR chairman Mohamad Hairul Amir Sabri as a senator reflects the strong and stable cooperation among its component parties.
Perak PKR information chief and spokesman Azam Afandi said the support was more than just a mandate for Hairul.
He said it showed that cooperation among the parties which form the state unity government remained harmonious.
"The full 33 votes from the government bloc not only gave a mandate to a candidate.
"More importantly, it once again demonstrated that the relationship and cooperation among the parties forming the unity government in Perak remain harmonious, strong and stable," he said in a statement today.
Perak's unity government comprises Barisan Nasional (nine seats) and Pakatan Harapan (24 seats), while Perikatan Nasional holds 26 seats.
Azam said political stability and the ability of the parties to work together based on mutual trust and the interests of the people were strengths that needed to be safeguarded.
He said this was particularly important amid an increasingly challenging political landscape.
"Perak PKR will continue to play a constructive role alongside all its unity government partners to ensure that the political stability enjoyed today is translated into effective administration, state development and the well-being of all Perak residents," he said.
He said the appointment carried a significant trust and responsibility, adding that Perak PKR was confident Mohamad Hairul would bring the voice and interests of the people of Perak to the Dewan Negara with integrity, wisdom and commitment.
Azam also thanked PKR's PH component partners, particularly DAP and Amanah, as well as its unity government partners from BN, for their trust and support.
He said continued cooperation among the parties was crucial to maintaining political stability while ensuring that the people remained the priority.
Earlier, at the state assembly sitting, Hairul was elected as the new senator representing Perak in the Dewan Negara.
The 38-year-old defeated Perak Pas Dewan Ulama chairman Muhammad Zulkifli Muhammad Zakaria, who was the other candidate for the seat.
A total of 59 votes were cast by members of the state assembly.
Hairul's nomination was proposed by Teja assemblyman Sandrea Ng Shy Ching (PKR) and seconded by Lintang assemblyman Datuk Mohd Zolkfaly Haron (BN).
The election was held following the expiry of the term of Perak PH chairman Datuk Seri Dr Mujahid Yusuf Rawa on May 24.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: As election looms, Sweden's government is paying immigrants to leave
Article:
ONCE known for its welcome to migrants, Sweden has not only shut its borders over the last decade, its right-wing government is now paying some foreign-born residents to leave, part of a tough stance on migration it hopes will help it secure reelection this month.
As countries across Europe clamp down on immigration, Sweden has made one of the most drastic about-turns. It took in 163,000 asylum seekers in 2015 - the second highest per capita in Europe.
By 2025, that number had fallen 96 per cent.
Since the start of 2026, the Swedish coalition government, which took power in 2022 on a pledge to cut immigration and crime, has been offering those with residency permits from outside the European Union up to 350,000 Swedish crowns (US$37,000) if they leave the country.
The scheme is being closely watched abroad, and strongly supported by the Sweden Democrats, a far-right party that is outside the government but backs it in parliament.
"Do you miss Mogadishu? The remigration grant will help you get home," reads an advert, paid for by the Sweden Democrats on a bus and aimed at Somali immigrants.
The government has publicised the programme in multiple languages on its websites. The scheme has a budget of 1.3 billion Swedish crowns.
Governments and political parties across Europe are watching as some also consider ways to send people back.
Anti-immigration rhetoric has surged since over a million people, mainly Syrians fleeing war, arrived in Europe in 2015.
That has given right-wing nationalist parties a boost, pushing governments to adopt increasingly restrictive migration policies focused on deterrence and returns.
Mary Khan-Hohloch, a European Parliament lawmaker for Alternative for Germany (AfD), which won 44 per cent of the vote in state elections in Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday, welcomed the Swedish initiative.
"Given the considerable financial and social burdens facing many European countries as a result of migration policies to date, interest in effective return and remigration programmes is likely to continue to grow," she told Reuters in an email.
However, Bram Frouws, director of the Mixed Migration Centre, a research body, said there was no evidence these kinds of schemes produce any significant increase in voluntary emigration.
"This is one of those policy proposals where this doesn't even matter, it's mainly symbolic, it's about signalling how tough they are on migration," he said.
So far this year, 171 people have taken up the offer of cash to leave. The Sweden Democrats want to extend the offer to immigrants with Swedish citizenship, if they agree to revoke it.
The opposition and civil rights groups have accused Kristersson of going too far and call the policy divisive.
Latest opinion polls for the Sept 13 election show an almost equal split between the government on one side and the Social Democrats and centre-left on the other in the country of 10.6 million, where two million are foreign-born.
In the working-class Stockholm suburb of Satra a dozen immigrants have gathered at a community centre to have coffee and practice Swedish.
Among them are a Sudanese woman, two people from Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine, one person who fled the Taliban in Afghanistan and a dissident from China.
They have all heard about the government cash incentive to leave. None are interested.
"I want freedom, to be able to work and live a good life," said Elena Ibrahim, 42, from Sudan. She fled her ex-husband and religious oppression eight years ago. Now remarried, she works as an artist. "I will not go back."
Mahmoud Khalfi, imam at the Stockholm Mosque, Sweden's largest, said the scheme and anti-immigrant rhetoric were divisive and caused anxiety among Sweden's Muslim population.
The policy, he said, "doesn't solve any problem. Even if a few thousand leave, it has made it worse for those who have to stay."
Sweden has also started tightening other rules for immigrants - no longer awarding permanent residency permits and making immigrants re-apply for them after three years.
In August, the government launched the first-ever citizenship tests, mandatory for all who apply.
"It wasn't that hard," said Cornelius, 38, originally from Cameroon, adding that citizenship would bring peace of mind.
"Sweden is a very good place. It's safe and there are jobs."
* The writer is from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: AI Governance Bill expected to be tabled in Parliament by Q1 2027 at the latest
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Artificial Intelligence (AI) Governance Bill being drafted by the Digital Ministry is expected to be tabled in Parliament this quarter or by the first quarter of next year at the latest, said Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo.
He said the draft bill had been completed after the ministry conducted workshops and engagement sessions to obtain views from stakeholders, and was now in the process of being submitted to the cabinet.
"The draft has already been completed. We have held workshops and so on, obtained views from everyone involved, and we are now in the process of submitting the paper to the cabinet.
"So, hopefully, it will be tabled in Parliament this quarter or, if not, in the first quarter of next year," he told reporters after launching the opening of Scars of War - An International Photography and Art Exhibition at the Lin Xiang Xiong Art Gallery today.
The two-month exhibition, which begins today, is an international cultural initiative bringing together humanitarian documentation and contemporary art to explore the continuing impact of armed conflicts on people.
It features 38 documentary photographs by Alison Locke, Cory Wright, Giovanni Diffidenti and Werner Anderson, alongside four original artworks by Prof Lin Xiang Xiong.
Previously, the ministry, through the National AI Office (NAIO), began engagement sessions throughout July to refine the proposed AI Governance Bill, as part of the government's efforts to introduce and enhance understanding of the governance framework that will form the basis for the proposed bill.
Gobind said AI governance was not solely focused on legislation, but involved three main aspects, namely standards, regulations and laws, with matters that could be addressed through standards already being implemented through the establishment of MY-AI Standards under the ministry, which is now collaborating with Sirim Bhd.
He said there were AI-related matters that required regulation but did not necessarily warrant legislation, and could therefore be addressed through regulations that could be implemented more quickly.
"For some of these matters, we look first at standards, then regulations and subsequently laws. The ability to formulate regulations is also important, given that AI technology is developing rapidly and new issues may arise at any time," he said.
He said the establishment of AI Malaysia was part of efforts to provide a structure to ensure compliance with the law and enable action to be taken in the event of violations.
"Efforts to establish the enforcement structure are now being pursued concurrently with the process of bringing the bill to the cabinet.
"This integrated approach is important to ensure that governance and enforcement mechanisms are in place when the bill is passed," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pilot's wife sends heartfelt message after husband's death in heli crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: "Alex, take care of Zainol until you reach heaven. Please keep an eye on Zainol if he starts acting up, okay?"
That was the message from Izzati Syamimi, wife of pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30, to her husband's friend, Alexson Adit Henry, 31, who was also killed in the helicopter crash at the STOLport in Long Lellang, Sarawak, two days ago.
Izzati left the message in the comments section of a Threads post by Alexson's wife, Stephanie Essah.
The
crash near the Long Lellang airbase
also claimed the lives of three Health Ministry personnel, including a medical officer and two nurses.
Stephanie had shared a family photo of herself, Alexson and their two children, Candy and Ivan.
"Our last photo together as a family. Thank you for everything, my love. Know that I will always love you, as will our children.
"Candy and Ivan love you very much. They are proud to have a father like you, our true hero. Fly high and rest in peace. See you again in another life. Love, from mummy," she said.
The post drew condolences and messages of support from other users.
"Such strong wives. My condolences, sis. May everything be made easier for all of you," said user @daadiiduu_aryanarissa.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: M360 Asean bridge differences, advance shared digital future - Fahmi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: M360 Asean can serve as a regional platform for governments and industry players with differing stances to convene, deliberate and identify common ground to advance Asean's digital future, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said Malaysia is in a unique position to bring together stakeholders who might otherwise be seen as poles apart, as reflected in the diverse lineup of partners and industry sponsors gathered at the event.
"Yet, through an event under the GSMA, we can all converse in a civilised fashion and find ways forward together," he said in his opening remarks at M360 Asean 2026 today.
Fahmi said that this is the very role envisioned for the event as governments, regulators and industry players navigate the opportunities and challenges arising from the region's digital transformation.
"This is what I believe M360 Asean can do, provide that space for us to meet, to think, to debate and to find ways forward together," he said.
He expressed hope that the collaboration forged through the event would deliver shared prosperity, noting that building a common Asean future would bring widespread benefits to communities across the region.
"Malaysia is not simply offering a market; we are offering a partnership. Our approach is to test solutions against real needs, measure what works and develop practical models with relevance beyond our borders," he said.
Touching on Asean's digital prospects, Fahmi said the effective implementation of the Asean Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA) could propel the regional digital economy to USD2 trillion by 2030.
However, he cautioned that this potential would not be realised automatically, as fragmented digital markets, access disparities and a lack of digital trust could impede investment, stifle growth and leave communities behind.
"The real measure of success is whether this regional ambition translates into practical opportunities across Asean," he said.
He said that wider digital inclusion must go hand in hand with robust safety measures, with trust serving as the cornerstone for citizens to use digital services confidently and for businesses to invest.
"Trust is not an obstacle to innovation. It is the foundation that allows people to participate safely, businesses to invest and digital services to grow sustainably," he added.
M360 Asean 2026, organised by the GSMA on Sept 9 and 10, brings together ministers, regulators and industry leaders to discuss digital trust, artificial intelligence, resilient infrastructure and regional digital integration.
The event, held for the first time in the Asean region and in Malaysia, is endorsed by the Communications Ministry, with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) as host partner. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Connectivity, public trust must advance together for inclusive digital Asean
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Echoing Malaysia's drive for an equitable and secure regional digital ecosystem, Asean nations must accelerate connectivity while bolstering public trust to ensure rural and remote communities are not left behind.
This shared priority was underscored by regional leaders during a panel session on digital connectivity and trust at the M360 Asean 2026 conference today, hosted in Malaysia as the country champions a unified and safe digital future for the bloc.
Indonesian Communication and Digital Affairs Ministry secretary-general Dr Ir Ismail said government intervention remained necessary in areas where building telecommunications infrastructure was not commercially viable for private operators.
"Infrastructure is a must and connectivity is a must because digital connectivity gives us opportunities to improve the economy and the prosperity of our people, including in education and health," he said.
Ismail said Indonesia's geographical complexity, encompassing more than 17,000 islands, required the government to support common infrastructure, including terrestrial networks and satellite connectivity.
Such open-access infrastructure, he noted, can be made available to telecommunications operators at minimal cost, allowing them to extend services to underserved areas while maintaining sustainable operations.
He said the Indonesian government was also managing spectrum costs and allowing infrastructure collaboration among operators to accelerate the expansion of 5G services.
Ismail said Indonesia's 5G coverage had reached about 50 per cent and would be progressively expanded from major cities to secondary cities and rural areas.
However, he said that physical connectivity alone is insufficient without strong public confidence to drive the adoption of online solutions, especially digital financial services.
"Trust is not the responsibility of the government alone. Collaboration among all stakeholders is needed to build that trust," he said.
Sharing a similar perspective, Timor-Leste National Communications Authority chairman Flavio Cardoso Neves said his country was prioritising connectivity, cybersecurity and public confidence in digital safety as it advanced its digital transformation.
"Connectivity is most important. We are talking about digitalisation, but without connectivity in rural areas, it will be difficult to ensure that all citizens have access," he said.
Neves said Timor-Leste was developing nationwide connectivity and submarine-cable infrastructure while learning from the experiences of fellow Aseaan countries, including Indonesia and Malaysia.
He said digital literacy would be crucial to ensuring that citizens used technology according to their needs and with a sense of responsibility.
M360 Asean 2026, organised by the GSMA (RPT: GSMA) on Sept 9 and 10, brings together ministers, regulators and industry leaders to discuss digital trust, artificial intelligence, resilient infrastructure and regional digital integration.
The event, held for the first time in the Asean region and in Malaysia, is endorsed by the Communications Ministry, with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) as host partner.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil launched the event this morning. — BERNAMA

Title: All UiTM endurance challenge patients allowed home, except one
Article:
MARAN: The sole endurance challenge participant initially treated in the Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Hospital (Hoshas) Intensive Care Unit (ICU) has been transferred to a general ward.
The student is among nine Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) students hospitalised after experiencing breathing difficulties during the Komander Kesatria Endurance Challenge at the UiTM Jengka campus on Sept 4. One participant
died
in the incident.
Maran police chief Superintendent Wong Kim Wai said the student received initial treatment at Jengka Hospital on Sept 4 before being transferred to the ICU at Hoshas alongside two other participants the following day.
Of the three students admitted to Hoshas, one died on Sept 5, while another was discharged on Sept 7. Six other participants treated at Jengka Hospital have also been discharged.
The student at Hoshas has been moved to a general ward and remains under observation, Wong said.
One participant, Fadhlan Fakhry Solana Mohd Fellimal, 21,
died
in the Hoshas ICU at 2pm on Sept 5. He was among three students transferred to Hoshas following the event.
The annual endurance event hosted by UiTM Jengka attracted 521 participants from UiTM campuses nationwide, except Sarawak.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Country Heights unit faces RM55mil asset auction
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Country Heights Holdings Bhd unit Country Heights Commercial Development Sdn Bhd (CHCD) faces a judicial auction of a 2.60-hectare commercial property in Kajang, Selangor, with a reserve price of RM55 million.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, Country Heights said the property was pledged as collateral for an S$11.5 million loan from CGS International Capital Singapore Pte Ltd.
Pursuant to High Court orders, the property is scheduled for an electronic public auction on Sept 21, 2026, at 9am, with a reserve price of RM55 million.
The latest reserve price represents a reduction of RM14.85 million, or 21.26 per cent, from the previous RM69.85 million reserve price.
The property was previously put up for auction on March 25 last year at RM69.85 million, but the auction was unsuccessful.
Country Heights said the property had a carrying value of about RM33.5 million based on CHCD's latest available financial statements.
"As the auction has yet to take place, the actual sale consideration and the resultant gain or loss arising from the property's disposal cannot be determined at this juncture," it said.
Country Heights said the scheduled auction is not expected to materially impact its day-to-day operations immediately, aside from the potential loss of property ownership if the auction succeeds.
The company will take further appropriate steps upon advice from its legal advisers, it added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nepal flood death toll tops 1,410 as search for survivors continues
Article:
KATHMANDU: Nepali rescuers clung to hopes of finding survivors trapped in hydropower tunnels on Wednesday, two weeks after deadly flooding triggered by a glacial mountain collapse.
The August 26 tsunami-like surge of water, mud and debris, which began on the China-Nepal border, has killed more than 1,410 people and left 5,651 missing.
"The rescue and search work in the tunnels at Trishuli 3A, 3B and Chilime hydropower projects is ongoing," Nepal Army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet told AFP.
In Nepal, 1,367 bodies have been recovered and 5,132 people are missing, its disaster authority said on Wednesday.
In China, 43 people are dead and 519 are missing, according to state media.
Hundreds of foreigners are among the missing, as well as hundreds of hydropower workers.
Three people were rescued from deep inside tunnels – two Nepalis on Friday and a Chinese man on Saturday.
But there has been no official confirmation of further survivors since then.
Authorities appealed on Wednesday for overseas family members of the missing – preferably parents or children – to submit DNA samples via email.
A public notice outlined specific types of genetic tests the family members should seek out depending on their sex and relationship to the missing person.
Thousands of people displaced by the disaster are living in camps, and the charity Save the Children said as many as 540 children had been separated from their parents.
Nepal police said they were taking extra care to ensure the safety of children and women in relief camps.
"We have become more vigilant in temporary holding centres in the affected areas where there are children, women or minority groups who could be victims of sexual abuse," said Nepal Police spokesman Abi Narayan Kafle.
"We have also started providing psychosocial counselling in different camps," he told AFP.
While the exact cause of the glacial collapse is unclear, climate change is accelerating glacial melt worldwide and increasing the risk of such disasters.
Nepal, a largely rural nation of 30 million people that has contributed little to the greenhouse gas emissions driving global warming, has said reconstruction could cost billions of dollars.
Kafle said security personnel have involved community members to search for bodies feared buried under debris.
"We have started a special search campaign for missing bodies all across the Bhotekoshi river corridor," he said.
"We are also using drones to search for bodies."--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Blackstone buys majority stake in South Korean logistics park
Article:
BENGALURU: Blackstone said on Thursday it has acquired a majority interest in Sanha Logistics Park II, a dry storage logistics development in South Korea, through a primary share issuance, as it seeks to deepen its presence in the East Asian nation.
Singapore-based real-estate manager ESR will remain an investor in the project and continue to serve as development manager and asset manager through its South Korean platform, ESR Kendall Square, the companies said.
Sanha Logistics Park II, a storage development spanning 334,000 square meters, is currently under construction and is expected to be completed in 2028.
The total development cost of Sanha Logistics Park II is approximately 600 billion Korean won (US$448.30 million), ESR told Reuters.
Blackstone did not specify the value of the stake.
The park is positioned along the Gyeongbu Expressway, Korea's main highway corridor connecting Seoul and Busan, and is expected to support warehouse automation and other evolving supply chain requirements, the companies said.
"This investment deepens Blackstone's presence in Korea and reinforces logistics as our high conviction real estate theme globally," said Chris Kim, head of Blackstone Real Estate-Korea.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Four Indonesian volcanoes record 13 eruptions as activity continues
Article:
JAKARTA: Four Indonesian volcanoes, including Anak Krakatau, recorded at least 13 eruptions on Thursday as volcanic activity continued across the archipelago, with ash from one volcano keeping an airport in East Nusa Tenggara closed.
The Volcanology and Geological Hazard Mitigation Centre (PVMBG) said as of midday, six eruptions were recorded at Mount Ibu in North Maluku, four at Ili Lewotolok in East Nusa Tenggara, two at Semeru in East Java and one at Anak Krakatau, which erupted at 9.10am Western Indonesian Time.
However, the eruption column at Anak Krakatau was not observed.
Earlier monitoring between midnight and 6am showed the volcano was covered by fog, with three hybrid or multiphase earthquakes and continuous tremor recorded during the period.
The volcano remained on Level III, the second-highest level in Indonesia's four-tier volcanic alert system.
Separately, the Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) said in an update on Instagram that volcanic ash from Anak Krakatau and Ili Lewotolok was no longer detected.
Ash from Mount Ibu was detected at up to 2.1 km, while Semeru could not be observed due to cloud cover.
The latest volcanic activity comes after volcanic ash from Anak Krakatau forced the temporary closure of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport and seven other airports earlier this week.
Meanwhile, AirNav Indonesia in a statement said Wunopito Airport in Lewoleba, East Nusa Tenggara, remained closed due to volcanic ash from Ili Lewotolok, with the closure extended until an estimated 7am local time on Friday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Techna-X admits listing breach over undisclosed RM45m Hong Kong asset sale
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Techna-X Bhd has admitted to breaching Bursa Malaysia's listing rules after failing to announce a previously executed RM45.0 million agreement to dispose of its 50 per cent stake in Hong Kong Aerospace Beidou New Energy Technology Co Ltd (HKAB).
In a response to Bursa's query filed on Thursday, the group revealed it had entered into a conditional share sale agreement (SSA) on Dec 30, 2025, with 71-year-old Chinese investor Nong You Hua.
Nong, who already holds a 15 per cent stake in HKAB, subsequently defaulted on payment terms, leading Techna-X to terminate the deal on July 10, 2026. Techna-X did not disclose the deal, as required under Chapter 10 of the Main Market Listing Requirements.
"The company confirms that it did not fully comply with Paragraph 10.06 (Immediate Announcement) and Paragraph 10.07 (Shareholders' Approval) under Part D, Chapter 10 of the MMLR at the material time, as the transaction was neither announced immediately upon execution nor submitted for prior shareholders' approval," it said in the filing.
Techna-X attributed its non-disclosure and failure to seek prior shareholder approval—despite a highest percentage ratio of 80.43 per cent—to an "administrative oversight".
The regulatory disclosure follows exchange inquiries after Techna-X entered into a second SSA on Sept 3 to sell the exact same 100,000 ordinary shares in HKAB for RM45.0 million to private entity Tess Global Sdn Bhd.
In announcing the current SSA, Techna-X noted that the disposal consideration was based on Tess Global's evaluation of the future potential in HKAB. However, Techna-X committed to appointing an independent valuation firm to appraise the value of HKAB.
The consideration makes up 141.69 per cent of Techna-X's audited consolidated net assets for the financial period ended Dec 31, 2025 of RM31.76 million.
Techna-X first invested in HKAB in October 2020, injecting RM41.66 million. The proposed disposal of the 50% stake in HKAB to Tess Global will give rise to an estimated net gain of RM19.74 million.
The group had earmarked RM30 million from the proceeds for the expansion of its food business through the opening of 10 new restaurants in Peninsular Malaysia.
The deal is expected to be completed in the second quarter of 2027, subject to shareholder approval at an extraordinary general meeting.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: North Korea leader's daughter believed to have younger sibling
Article:
SEOUL: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un's daughter and apparent successor is believed to have a younger sibling, South Korea's spy agency said on Thursday, offering a more detailed view of the ruling family's structure.
Seoul's spy agency has previously said Kim is believed to have three children, but there has been uncertainty about their order of birth.
Kim's daughter, Kim Ju Ae, was first introduced to the public in 2022 when she accompanied her father to the launch of an intercontinental ballistic missile.
The Kim family has ruled North Korea with an iron grip for decades, and a cult of personality surrounding their "Paektu bloodline" dominates daily life in the diplomatically isolated country.
"The National Intelligence Service currently assesses that Kim Ju Ae is being groomed as the successor and understands she has a younger sibling of unknown gender," the agency said in a statement.
The NIS added that it was continuing to verify whether Kim Ju Ae has an older brother, but believes that "even if he exists, he is not in a position to become the successor."
Since 2022, Kim Ju Ae has appeared at a number of major political events with the North Korean leader, including a high-profile visit to Beijing.
North Korean state media have also referred to her as "the beloved child" and a "great person of guidance" – "hyangdo" in Korean – a term typically reserved for top leaders and their successors.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cops need months of intelligence to bust drug lab syndicates
Article:
BACHOK: Operations to dismantle drug syndicates, particularly those involving clandestine drug laboratories, require months of intelligence gathering to ensure the entire network is uncovered before raids are carried out.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said police took time to track how precursor chemicals brought into the country were being used to manufacture drugs.
He said the chemicals had to be traced from their point of entry, including major ports such as Port Klang, to their final destinations.
"When precursor chemicals arrive in the country, we need to trace where they are taken, as they usually transit through several locations.
"At the same time, we need to identify those involved and determine what they are producing.
"That is why intelligence gathering can take months, until we are certain that the activity involves a drug laboratory before raids and arrests are carried out," he told reporters after visiting the Bachok National Anti-Drug Agency (Nada) rehabilitation centre here today.
Also present was Nada director-general Datuk Ruslin Jusoh.
Hussein said gathering intelligence was complex and required continuous monitoring of suspected individuals and locations.
"We need extensive intelligence gathering and surveillance, particularly in industrial areas, which can be vast and make it difficult to identify premises being used as clandestine drug laboratories.
"Acting too early can also jeopardise an investigation, as police may only manage to arrest one or two people, or a transporter, without uncovering the actual location of the drug laboratory serving as the syndicate's operational hub.
"Operations and raids not only expose the existence of clandestine drug laboratories, but also lead to the arrest of a large portion of the syndicate members involved," he said.
It was reported yesterday that a large-scale drug syndicate was dismantled after police seized 13.17 tonnes of synthetic drugs worth RM2.41 billion in a raid on a factory converted into a drug laboratory in Bandar Puncak Alam, Selangor, last month.
Police detected the syndicate following
six months of intelligence gathering
based on the delivery addresses of the chemicals, which eventually led them to the premises in Bandar Puncak Alam.
The laboratory is believed to have been operating for about a year.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pakistan says no military response discussed under Mecca pact over Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
Article:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan said on Thursday that there were no discussions about a military reaction from Islamabad under the Mecca agreement in response to the Houthis' attacks on Saudi Arabia, but added that Pakistan will "act" when the "time comes."
The comments by Pakistan's foreign ministry spokesperson came in response to a question on how Islamabad plans to fulfill its obligations under a joint defence accord it signed with Turkiye and Saudi Arabia.
The joint defence agreement signed last month stipulates that an armed attack on any one of the three countries will be regarded as an attack on all of them.
"There is no such thing under discussion right now ... When time comes (we) will act under the agreement," foreign ministry spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said at a weekly media briefing.
There are also no plans to expand the Mecca alliance at this moment, Khan added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Online scam committee findings heading to cabinet soon - Fahmi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Findings from a series of discussions by a special working committee tackling online scams will be presented to the cabinet soon, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said.
He said a cabinet note was being prepared to outline several key decisions reached following the committee's engagements.
"The working committee has held a series of discussions, and I will submit a cabinet note soon to inform the cabinet of several decisions," he told reporters after launching M360 Asean 2026 today.
Fahmi described the committee as unique as it brings together commercial banks, telecommunications companies and digital platform providers, including TikTok, for the first time in a coordinated effort to combat online scams.
He said discussions also examined potential gaps in existing laws and ways to strengthen strategic cooperation among enforcement agencies involved in investigating scam cases.
The cross-agency cooperation involves the Attorney-General's Chambers and the police's Commercial Crime Investigation Department.
The working committee and a special technical group were previously established to coordinate efforts by the government, regulators, enforcement agencies, financial institutions, telecommunications companies, and digital platforms in tackling online scams.
Earlier in his opening speech, Fahmi noted that four major operations targeting the possession and distribution of child sexual abuse material (CSAM) since December 2024 had resulted in 117 arrests across 162 locations.
A total of over 1.47 million digital files were recovered during the crackdown, of which 204,934 were confirmed to be child sexual abuse material.
To curb such crimes, he said Malaysia is bolstering its digital safety framework through the Online Safety Act 2025 (ONSA), the Child Protection Code and the Risk Mitigation Code.
These frameworks impose clear responsibilities on platform providers, encompassing child safety-by-design, age verification, proactive risk assessments, stringent content governance and responsive reporting mechanisms.
M360 Asean 2026, organised by the GSMA on Sept 9 and 10, brings together ministers, regulators and industry leaders to discuss digital trust, artificial intelligence, resilient infrastructure and regional digital integration.
The event, held for the first time in the Asean region and in Malaysia, is endorsed by the Communications Ministry, with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) as host partner.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Sarawak Flying Doctor Service suspended after helicopter crash
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: All Flying Doctor Service (FDS) operations in Sarawak have been temporarily suspended following a helicopter crash involving an aircraft used for the service in Long Lellang.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the suspension would allow investigations and reviews of safety and operational mechanisms to be carried out by the relevant parties.
"Medical evacuation services for emergency cases will continue through cooperation between the Health Ministry (MoH) and the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department.
"At the same time, the MoH will hold further discussions with the armed forces to explore the use of its assets to ensure patients requiring emergency treatment can be transferred to appropriate healthcare facilities," he said in a statement today.
Dzulkefly said the MoH would conduct a comprehensive assessment of the overall FDS service delivery framework in Sarawak, including contracts, governance, operational safety, coverage requirements and the effectiveness of the existing service delivery model.
He said the assessment aimed to ensure that the approach to be implemented in the future would be safer, resilient, sustainable and responsive to the healthcare needs of communities in rural Sarawak.
"The MoH is reassessing the locations and methods of access to FDS services, including alternative transport and other safe and practical approaches to ensure communities in rural areas continue to have access to healthcare services," he said.
He said the MoH understood the difficulties and challenges that might arise following the temporary suspension.
"However, the safety of personnel and patients remains the MoH's priority, while ensuring the continuity of healthcare services for communities in rural areas.
"The MoH will continue to monitor the situation from time to time and provide the public with the latest developments as appropriate," he said.
Yesterday, Dzulkefly said the government would
continue operating FDS
to ensure healthcare coverage for remote communities.
In Tuesday's incident, a BO-105 helicopter crashed at Long Lellang Airport in Ulu Baram, Sarawak.
The crash claimed the lives of Captain Zainol Afiq Sham Bee; medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin; medical assistant Alexson Adit; and two nurses, Debra Moset and Jessie Paya, who were travelling to Long Lellang to provide healthcare services to the local community.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Azam: Tei's lock-up attire, handcuffs complied with MACC procedures
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief commissioner Tan Sri Azam Baki maintained that requiring businessman Albert Tei to wear lock-up attire and handcuffs complied with prescribed procedures and was not unconstitutional.
In an affidavit replying to Tei's originating summons, Azam, who retired in May, said the requirement was governed by MACC Chief Commissioner's Directive No. 2/2020 on the Use of Lock-ups and Handcuffs.
He said the directive required detainees to wear MACC lock-up clothing at MACC offices and when taken out for investigations or court proceedings, including remand hearings where detainees must be handcuffed.
Azam maintained that the requirement applied to all detainees and was not imposed specifically on Tei.
Both requirements applied to Tei after a remand order was obtained against him on Nov 30, 2025, when he was taken to five locations in Bandar Puteri Puchong, Taman Kinrara, Taman Kuchai Jaya, Jalan Desa Bakti and Damansara Perdana for searches.
Azam added that the MACC was not responsible for the media publicity surrounding photographs of Tei in lock-up attire during his court remand process.
He said the lock-up attire procedure was prescribed under a directive issued pursuant to Section 12 of the MACC Act 2009.
Azam said there was no issue of illegality or unconstitutionality as alleged, as the requirement complied with the law.
He said the directive did not contravene Article 5(1) of the Federal Constitution regarding personal liberty, as wearing lock-up attire was procedural and did not equate to a finding of guilt.
He added that there was no breach of Article 8(1) on equality because the rule was procedural and applied generally, noting that Tei had failed to explain how the clause was breached beyond calling the requirement unreasonable.
Azam said the suit should be dismissed, adding that Federal Counsel would present legal submissions during the hearing.
Tei's lawyer, Mahajoth Singh, said the Special Powers Division High Court has fixed Oct 26 to hear the matter.
In January, Tei filed the suit at the High Court against the MACC, Azam and the government, alleging that he was forced to wear an orange lock-up shirt while under investigation.
Tei was seeking a court declaration that the action was unconstitutional, as well as damages to be assessed by the court.
Tei questioned why prominent individuals such as former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, his wife and others were not made to wear the same attire, alleging double standards in enforcement.
He claimed that MACC had effectively passed judgment before a court decision and challenged the agency to explain its legal basis and provide statistics on those arrested, made to wear orange lock-up attire and later acquitted.
Another lawyer representing Tei, N. Surendran, questioned the legal basis for forcing someone merely under investigation to wear lock-up attire, adding that widely circulated photographs of Tei gave the impression he was already guilty.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Petronas moves to unlock stranded oil, accelerate exploration & production
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) is stepping up efforts to unlock Malaysia's marginal and stranded hydrocarbon resources, with two new upstream initiatives aimed at accelerating exploration and production.
Through Malaysia Petroleum Management (MPM), Petronas has awarded the Estuary Cluster small field asset production sharing contract (SFA PSC) to Harvester Energy (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd, while handing over seismic data for the Mutiara Cluster to support further exploration.
The Estuary Cluster comprises the Lerek, Korbu and Diwangsa fields in the Malay Basin, one of Malaysia's established offshore hydrocarbon provinces, it said in a statement.
The cluster is being developed around a technology-led concept that uses shallow-water subsea infrastructure to bring marginal oil resources into production.
The approach is designed to shorten the timeline to first commercial production while reducing capital expenditure and the physical footprint associated with conventional field development.
It would also support the reuse and redeployment of production infrastructure, in line with Petronas' efforts to enable innovative and commercially viable solutions for Malaysia's small field assets.
MPM senior vice-president Datuk Ir Dr Bacho Pilong said the Estuary Cluster PSC award reflected Petronas' continued focus on unlocking discovered resources through innovative and fit-for-purpose development solutions.
"By introducing technology-led approaches, we are opening new pathways to monetise small and stranded fields that may otherwise remain undeveloped," he said.
The award marks Harvester's entry into Malaysia's upstream sector and reinforces the country's position as an attractive destination for agile and technology-focused energy players seeking small field development opportunities.
The Estuary Cluster was offered through Malaysia Bid Round Plus (MBR+), which complements the annual Malaysia Bid Round by providing investors with year-round access to selected upstream opportunities, as well as technical data through Petronas myPROdata.
Meanwhile, MPM has handed over an enhanced 3D seismic dataset to Dialog Resources Sdn Bhd for the Mutiara Cluster, located off the east coast of Sabah.
The handover marks a step towards progressing the cluster's development towards production and advancing discovered resources in the Sandakan Basin.
Bacho said the delivery of the enhanced dataset marked MPM's first acquisition of new 3D seismic data over an area that already had existing coverage.
"The improved subsurface imaging will enable Dialog to better evaluate Mutiara Cluster's resources and support East Sabah's long-term energy security," he said.
The Mutiara Cluster comprises five discovered marginal oil and gas fields - Nymphe, Nymphe North, Kuda Terbang, Benrinnes and Mutiara Hitam.
Dialog was awarded the cluster under an SFA PSC during Malaysia Bid Round 2025, with first production targeted for 2029.
Development efforts are also focused on optimising project costs and accelerating the first gas date, supported by the sharing of information and technical proposals to advance the cluster's development.
These efforts are complemented by ongoing collaboration with Sabah state agencies to foster development synergies and stakeholder alignment in support of the state's East Coast long-term energy growth.
Petronas said the Estuary Cluster PSC award and Mutiara Cluster seismic data handover demonstrated its broader approach to strengthening Malaysia's upstream proposition by widening access to investment opportunities and enabling discovered resources to progress towards production more efficiently.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Asean eyes single submission model for medical device approval
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The proposed Asean Single Submission Model for the pre-market approval of medical devices could move towards implementation once member states agree to the initiative.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the proposal is currently being put forward as an agenda item, with Asean countries contributing input and sharing best practices on its implementation.
"During the side event (of the 17th Asean Health Ministers Meeting (AHMM) and Related Meetings), we received very good input and best practices. The Philippines, in particular, suggested that we should have a system that is connected and interoperable," he said at a press conference after launching the Asean Strategic Health Agenda (ASHA) 2026-2030 programme today.
Dzulkefly said establishing an interoperable system across all 11 Asean member states would take time as countries are at different stages of development, with some still working on their regulatory and legal frameworks while others, including Singapore and the Philippines, are more advanced.
He said member states had yesterday agreed in principle to support a phased Single Submission Model for the pre-market approval of medical devices, with Malaysia serving as the coordinating entry point for technical dossiers.
He said the agreement was reached during the inaugural Asean Roundtable Discussion on Medical Devices, which he chaired as part of specialised technical sessions held in conjunction with the 17th AHMM.
On bilateral engagements, Dzulkefly said Malaysia had reinforced its Memorandum of Understanding on Health Cooperation with Singapore, expanding collaboration in digital health, active ageing and regulatory reliance between the Medical Device Authority and Singapore's Health Sciences Authority.
He said Malaysia and Indonesia had also advanced initiatives in digital health, Traditional and Complementary Medicine and cross-border healthcare, with Malaysia's medical tourism sector recording more than RM2.2 billion in revenue in 2025.
He added that he looked forward to strategic bilateral sessions with China and Japan to further expand technical and investment ties.
"The 17th AHMM also marks a major diplomatic milestone with the inaugural Asean-United States and Asean-Japan Health Ministers' Meetings, alongside high-level consultations with China, the Republic of Korea and the World Health Organisation (WHO)," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar, Kelantan MB discuss stronger ties
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim met Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud to discuss ways to strengthen ties between the federal government and the opposition Pas-ruled state.
In a social media post, Anwar said the meeting covered federal support in several areas, including infrastructure, the economy, agriculture, education, healthcare and social amenities.
"We discussed efforts to strengthen cooperation and solidarity between the Federal and state governments.
"(This is) including support in various sectors, such as infrastructure, the economy, agriculture, education, healthcare and social amenities to ensure the state's development continues smoothly," said Anwar.
He said the cooperation would continue to be strengthened for the benefit and wellbeing of the people of Kelantan.
"Insya-Allah, this cooperation will continue to be strengthened in the interests and for the wellbeing of the people of Kelantan," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: King presents appointment letters to two judges
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, today presented instruments of appointment to two judges at Istana Negara.
The ceremony began with the presentation to Court of Appeal judge Alice Loke Yee Ching, followed by High Court judge Elaine Yap Chin Gaik.
Present were Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said, Chief Justice Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh, Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar, Court of Appeal President Datuk Seri Abu Bakar Jais, Chief Judge of Malaya Datuk Seri Hashim Hamzah and Chief Judge of Sabah and Sarawak Datuk Azizah Nawawi.
Loke, 64, was appointed Senior Federal Counsel in 2013, a position she held until 2018. She was appointed a judicial commissioner of the Shah Alam High Court on July 10, 2020.
She was elevated to Shah Alam High Court judge on Jan 17, 2023, before being appointed to the Kuala Lumpur High Court's Special Powers Division on Aug 18, 2025.
As a Kuala Lumpur High Court judge, Loke handled Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak's judicial review application over an alleged addendum order allowing the former prime minister to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
During her tenure as Senior Federal Counsel, Loke was involved in several high-profile cases, including admiralty proceedings at the Kuala Lumpur High Court to seize the Equanimity, a vessel allegedly built using funds from 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB).
She also handled the Sulu claim and lawsuits filed against the Malaysian government over the disappearance of Malaysia Airlines flight MH370.
Meanwhile, Yap, 53, holds a Bachelor of Laws from the University of Sydney and a Diploma in International Arbitration from the Chartered Institute of Arbitrators.
She was appointed a judicial commissioner of the Shah Alam High Court on Aug 28, 2024, before taking up the same position at the Kuala Lumpur High Court on Nov 3, 2025.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: HE Group secures RM25mil power systems order
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: HE Group Bhd's unit Hexatech Engineering Sdn Bhd has received a purchase order valued at RM25 million.
The order is for power distribution system works for a manufacturer involved in assembling, testing and packing of NAND flash memory products.
The purchase order commences on the date of acceptance and is targeted for completion in 20 weeks.
Barring any unforeseen circumstances, the purchase order is expected to contribute positively toward HE Group's future earnings and will not affect the group's share capital or substantial shareholders.
"The board, after due consideration, is of the opinion that the purchase order is in the best interest of the company," it said.
At 3pm, HE Group's shares rose one sen or 1.1 per cent to 92 sen, valuing the company at RM404.8 million.

Title: King grants audience to higher education minister, PSC chairman
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: His Majesty, Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia today granted an audience to Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir at Istana Negara.
According to a post on Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar's official Facebook page, during the audience session, His Majesty agreed to be presented with the current developments of the Sultan Ibrahim Malay Studies Chair at Beijing Foreign Studies University (BFSU).
Meanwhile, in a separate post, His Majesty also granted an audience to the Chairman of the Public Service Commission (PSC) Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Jailani Muhamed Yunus at Istana Negara.
Meanwhile, Zambry in a Facebook post said the Sultan Ibrahim Malay Studies Chair at BFSU reflects His Majesty's concern and patronage towards efforts to expand studies and strengthen the position of the Malay language, culture and civilisation on the international stage.
"May all of His Majesty's advice and views serve as a guide in further strengthening the field of Malay Studies and expanding the knowledge network between Malaysia and the world. Daulat Tuanku," he hailed.
