Title: 'I would give my life to bring them back,' man loses wife, two sons in Kluang fire
Article:
KLUANG: "I would give my life to bring them back."
Those were the heartbreaking words of Khairul Nizam Wahid, 50, who lost his wife and two sons after fire engulfed their double-storey terrace house in Taman Titiwangsa last night.
His wife, Noraini Ibrahim, 49, and sons Khairul Nurhaziqq Khairul Nizam, 18, and Khairul Nurhadif, 11, were found dead after the blaze broke out at 10.30pm.
Khairul Nizam said he had returned home after going out for a drink with a neighbour when he saw the sofa in the living room on fire.
"I tried to pull it out but failed as the flames caught on and quickly spread.
"I tried to get back inside because my wife and two sons were upstairs, unaware that the ground floor was on fire," he said when met outside Enche' Besar Hajjah Khalsom Hospital today.
He said Noraini later called him after hearing the commotion downstairs.
"I told her, 'The house is on fire.' After that, I could no longer hear their voices.
"I did everything I could to save them, but it was too late," he said.
Khairul Nizam said he was forced to leave through the kitchen door when thick smoke made it impossible to re-enter the house.
He then
alerted
neighbours, who rushed out to help and called the Fire and Rescue Department.
The couple ran a catering business.
He said they were earlier preparing several orders, including one for a school, for Maulidur Rasul celebrations tomorrow and Saturday.
"I don't know how I will face this. I tried my best to save them, but Allah loved them more.
"If I could, I would give my life instead. I wanted to climb upstairs, but the staircase was gone.
"I don't want to lose them. We were very close and never apart," he said.
Khairul Nizam said he had been told that his two sons were found embracing each other, with their mother lying beside them.
"I am sad because there will be no one left to scold me. My life is lonely now. I have lost them forever," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Umno Youth wants government to reintroduce GST
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government has been urged to immediately reinstate the Goods and Services Tax (GST), as the system is more transparent and efficient than the Sales and Services Tax (SST).
Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh said available data showed that revenue collected under the abolished tax system was significantly higher.
"If DAP representatives themselves are now brave enough to mention GST, why is the prime minister still afraid of these three letters?
"But it is all right, Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Umno Youth thanks you. There is nothing wrong with turning back when we eventually return to the right path.
"Even if you want to call it Madani Tax, go ahead. We are not like the Opposition during your time as opposition leader. If something is good, we support it. If it is not good, we will oppose it," Dr Akmal said in his policy speech at the opening of the Umno Youth delegates' conference here today.
It was previously reported that Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had said the government was open to studying the need to combine SST and GST to improve the country's tax system and make it more progressive.
Dr Akmal said the government's announcement that it was prepared to study a system combining the best elements of both tax systems clearly showed that the "door had been opened."
"If previously the door was firmly shut but today it is being opened little by little, what else can it be called other than a change in position? And most recently, DAP's Kepong MP Lim Lip Eng himself suggested that GST be reinstated if it was more effective than SST.
"He said the government did not need to create a complicated hybrid system simply to avoid the name GST," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Over 100 PPR tenants on eviction list, but Penang government not cruel'
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: More than 100 tenants of the Taman Manggis People's Housing Project (PPR) units are on the eviction list after losing eligibility for Penang's PPR housing.
The Penang government, however, said it was not acting cruelly.
State Housing and Environment Committee chairman Datuk S. Sundarajoo said the cases were carefully assessed and genuine hardship would be considered on a case-by-case basis.
"We are not a cruel government. We understand our people's problems and we know whether a case is genuine or not," he told newsmen here today.
Sundarajoo said 103 names were currently in the process of being dealt with in phases, with affected tenants still given opportunities to appeal and submit supporting documents.
He said the state had also granted extensions to tenants facing genuine difficulties, including those who were elderly, disabled or had already purchased homes that were still under construction.
"We go down to the PPR housing and give them an opportunity to appeal and undergo the verification process. If they come to us, it is not a problem," he said.
Sundarajoo said the state could not allow PPR units to remain occupied indefinitely by tenants who were no longer eligible, especially when many families were still without proper housing.
He cited Taman Manggis as an example, saying some units had been occupied for as long as 20 years and had been extensively renovated and fitted with air-conditioning, with tenants who have other luxuries such as high-end vehicles and superbikes.
He said the state had offered rent-to-own options to some affected tenants, while also giving them additional time to move.
"We cannot keep extending it because there are many people outside who do not have a home," he added.
On Tuesday, it was reported that seven more Taman Manggis PPR units were sealed, days after Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow defended the sealing of five units.
According to Pannir Selvam, who claimed to be Taman Manggis PPR residents' association chairman, affected residents were
scrambling for temporary accommodation
.
Sundarajoo also defended the state's broader housing programmes, saying Penang had achieved 176,457 units, or 80.21 per cent, of its 220,000-unit housing target by 2030.
He said the state had also purchased 1,133 units through its trust fund, involving RM49.26 million, for rent-to-own schemes aimed at helping lower-income families overcome the difficulty of raising housing deposits.
On claims that former tenants of Taman Manggis had previously been promised an opportunity to purchase their units, Sundarajoo said the state had found no documentary evidence supporting the allegation.
"If there is a black-and-white document, show it to me and I will allow the purchase," he said, stressing that verbal claims were insufficient.
He said the state had conducted background checks on affected households and had evidence showing some no longer met the eligibility requirements.
"We have all the evidence. We just do not want to tarnish anyone's name," he said.
Sundarajoo said PPR housing was intended for those genuinely unable to afford a home, adding that eligible tenants should use the available period to improve their economic circumstances or consider the state's rent-to-own schemes.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sarawak heli crash: Remains of Alexson to be brought Desa Senadin after post-mortem
Article:
MIRI: The family of the late medical assistant, Alexson Adit Henry, 31, who died in the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang on Tuesday is still awaiting the results of the autopsy before setting a date and time for his last respects and burial.
The deceased's sister, Annastasia Luyah Henry, through a post on her Facebook page, said the family would provide further details on the matter as soon as the autopsy results are obtained from the hospital.
"The deceased will be taken to his residence in Desa Senadin here after the autopsy process is completed," she said on behalf of Alexson's wife, Stephanie Essah Incham and all family members.
On Tuesday, the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) announced that a
BO-105 helicopter carrying five people
including the pilot, crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport (STOLport).
Apart from Alexson, the other
victims who died
were pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30, medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33, and two nurses, Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Four Chinese nationals face kidnapping charge after Singaporean allegedly held for RM3.28m ransom
Article:
BALIK PULAU, Sept 10 — Four Chinese nationals were charged at the Sessions Court here today with kidnapping a Singaporean man in July and demanding a ransom of SGD1 million (about RM3.28 million).
The accused, Liu Ting Jun, 46; Huang Jian, 39; Wang Hao Yu, 32; and Guan Siqi, 24, the only woman among them, however, pleaded not guilty after the charge was read to them in Mandarin before Judge Ahzal Fariz Ahmad Khairuddin.
According to the charge sheet, the accused, as well as two others still at large and another two individuals who have since died, are accused of jointly abducting and wrongfully confining Quek Aik Teng at the Penang International Airport in Bayan Lepas at 4.15 pm on July 26.
The charge is framed under Section 3(1) of the Kidnapping Act 1961, read together with Section 34 of the Penal Code, which provides for imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years, and caning, upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Ikmal Affendi Zulkifly did not offer bail on the grounds that the case involved a serious offence and is a matter of public interest.
“A review of their passports is being carried out, and there is still no confirmation from the Immigration Department of Malaysia,” he said.
Counsel Azizul Hilmi Zulkifli, representing Guan, Huang and Wang, asked the court to consider bail with additional conditions, such as surrendering their passports, reporting to the nearest police station, and not interfering with prosecution witnesses.
Meanwhile, counsel Edward Ng, representing Liu, sought reasonable bail on the grounds that his client had cooperated with the police throughout the investigation and had no prior criminal record.
The judge dismissed all the bail applications and set Oct 15 for further mention of the case.
It was previously reported that police had shot dead two foreign nationals in Alor Setar, Kedah, last Saturday.
The suspects were believed to be members of a kidnapping syndicate that targeted foreign nationals, luring them with job offers and holiday packages after befriending them through dating apps and social media. — Bernama

Title: Drug syndicates use public as mules to smuggle cannabis to Europe, says Bukit Aman
Article:
BACHOK,  Sept 10 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) have found that drug trafficking syndicates operating by air to Europe frequently use members of the public as drug mules, particularly to transport cannabis flowers, which are in high demand on the continent.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department Director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said, however, that not all pilots arrested for involvement in drug smuggling were transporting drugs to Europe.
“As far as we know, only one or two pilots were involved. Among them was a co-pilot arrested in Jakarta, Indonesia.
“To our knowledge, he (the co-pilot) travelled to Australia and Indonesia, not Europe. Smuggling to Europe mostly involves drug mules from the general public,” he told reporters during a press conference following a strategic visit to the Bachok Narcotics Rehabilitation Centre (Puspen) today.
He said most air-based drug trafficking cases involving Europe centred on cannabis flowers due to the high demand for the illicit substance in the market.
He urged the public to be wary of offers from syndicates promising lucrative payments, including free flight tickets or holiday packages, or asking them to transport certain luggage overseas.
“Our citizens need to understand that it is unusual for someone to offer large sums of money to cover tickets, holiday packages and the like.
“So, do not get ensnared by these syndicates,” he said.
On how drug trafficking syndicates manage to bypass security controls at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), Hussein said he could not elaborate as the Home Ministry is currently reviewing measures to strengthen security at all the country’s entry and exit points.
He said drug trafficking syndicates were becoming increasingly sophisticated and were exploiting various routes, including air, sea and land.
“If not by air, they use waterways, land routes and so on,” he said.
Hussein said that apart from Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), PDRM had also recorded arrests linked to drug smuggling activities at Sultan Azlan Shah Airport in Ipoh.
Yesterday, Bernama reported that police had detained a man to assist in investigations into the drug-related arrest of a Malaysian co-pilot in Jakarta, Indonesia, last July.
The co-pilot was detained by Indonesian authorities at Terminal 3 of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport on suspicion of attempting to smuggle 25 kilogrammes (kg) of drugs.
The Indonesian National Police (POLRI) subsequently found 15 packages containing 70,114 ecstasy pills and methamphetamine, with an estimated value of RM45 million. — Bernama

Title: Layang-Layang Aerospace voluntarily grounds BO-105 fleet after Sarawak helicopter crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Layang-Layang Aerospace Sdn Bhd has voluntarily grounded its entire fleet of BO 105 helicopters and other aircraft powered by Rolls-Royce 250-series engines as a precautionary safety measure following the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Sarawak two days ago that claimed five lives.
Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) chief executive officer Datuk Captain Norazman Mahmud said the decision was taken by the operator voluntarily and should not be interpreted as an indication of technical failure.
“I wish to stress that this grounding is precautionary. It is a precautionary safety measure taken by the operator. It should not be interpreted as an indication that the engine or any other particular component caused the accident,” he told reporters at the Malaysia Aviation Safety Seminar (MASS) 2026, here today.
Norazman said CAAM records showed that the helicopter’s Certificate of Airworthiness was valid until Aug 4, 2027, while its Certificate of Registration remained valid until July 28, 2029.
Addressing concerns over the aircraft’s operational lifespan, he said age alone did not determine airworthiness as long as the aircraft was properly maintained and continued to meet all maintenance protocols.
“From an airworthiness perspective, age alone is not a determining factor, provided the aircraft is properly maintained in accordance with its approved maintenance program and continues to meet all applicable airworthiness requirements,” he said.
Norazman said CAAM was monitoring the operator’s grounding and inspection programme, while also verifying the relevant regulatory, operator and pilot records.
The Air Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) under the Transport Ministry is independently investigating the crash.
“Any confirmed findings concerning the cause of the accident must come from AAIB following a thorough examination of the evidence. AAIB is responsible for establishing the circumstances, contributing factors, and cause of the accident...and CAAM is fully cooperating with the investigation and providing all relevant records,” he said.
Norazman urged the public and media to refrain from speculating on the cause of the crash before the investigation was completed.
“At this stage, it would be premature to speculate on whether the accident was caused by a technical issue, weather conditions, human factors, or any other factors,” he said.
On whether the operator had any previous history of air crashes, Norazman said CAAM would review its official records before releasing further details.
He added that in accordance with International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Annex 13 standards, AAIB would issue a preliminary investigation report within 30 days of the incident, followed by a final report within one year.
The BO-105 helicopter, operating a FDS mission, crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-off and Landing Airport (STOLport) in Ulu Baram, about 929 kilometres from Kuching last Tuesday, killing all five people onboard, including the 30-year-old pilot, Capt Zainol Afiq Bee Sham.
The other four were medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33; medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry, 31; and nurses Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44. — Bernama

Title: PAS at Umno assembly: Friendly visit or ‘preview’ of next election?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — When PAS delegates began arriving at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur last night for Umno’s annual assembly this week, the gesture drew more than polite greetings from party members.
For some Umno delegates, the presence of PAS delegates was a sign that the idea of Malay-Muslim unity was gaining ground again.
For others, it was a matter of returning a courtesy after Umno representatives attended PAS’s
muktamar
last week.
But even those who played down the symbolism acknowledged that the appearance of PAS figures at Umno’s biggest annual gathering carried a different weight this time, coming after Umno and PAS-backed cooperation in Johor and Negri Sembilan and as Melaka emerges as the next electoral test.
Muhamad Ainnul Haziq Mohd Razlan, 28, Kepong Umno division member, said he believed Umno should continue pursuing “
penyatuan ummah
”, or Malay-Muslim political unity, rather than treating it as a temporary political slogan.
“I think we should continue with this unity, and I hope the leaders, the top leadership, will make the best use of this unity. We at the youth level see this unity as something very good,” he told
Malay Mail
on the sidelines of the assembly.
Kepong Umno division member Muhamad Ainnul Haziq Mohd Razlan, 28, speaks during an interview with Malay Mail on the sidelines of the 2026 Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre in Kuala Lumpur, September 10, 2026. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
For Ainnul, PAS’s decision to send representatives to the Umno assembly was also a positive signal after Umno was invited to attend PAS’s
muktamar
last week.
“When PAS invited us to its
muktamar
last week, that was very good. When someone shows us kindness, we return it,” he said.
He said Umno Youth had also invited PAS Youth representatives to its programmes, describing the exchanges as a positive signal for possible cooperation in the 16th general election.
“Officially, we have to leave that to the top leadership and wait for their answer,” he said.
During the youth assembly on this morning, party youth chief Datuk Dr Akmal Saleh welcomed his compatriot from PAS, Afnan Hamimi Taib, describing the latter’s attendance as the culmination of three years of discussions between the two youth wings on national issues.
The distinction, between what members can read into the gestures and what the leadership is prepared to formally commit to, runs through conversations at this year’s assembly.
Hirzan Alam, 29, information chief of the Kota Kemuning Umno Youth division, took a more restrained view, saying PAS’s presence was mainly about returning the favour after Umno representatives attended its
muktamar
.
Kota Kemuning Umno Youth information chief Hirzan Alam, 29, shares his views with Malay Mail during the 2026 Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre in Kuala Lumpur, September 10, 2026. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
For Muhammad Najeeh Norazam, 33, a committee member of Umno Youth’s Damansara division, however, the visit could be read as something more.
“To be frank, if you ask me whether PAS coming to any party is more or less a formality to celebrate the relationship, like how we used to invite Harapan to come to WTC to establish unity and whatnot, it is basically more or less a symbolic indicator that we are working together,” he said.
Damansara Umno Youth committee member Muhammad Najeeh Norazam speaks to Malay Mail on the opening day of the 2026 Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre in Kuala Lumpur, September 9, 2026. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
Najeeh pointed to Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s position that the two parties currently have only a “mutual understanding”, rather than a formal agreement.
“But I think, for a fact, it is a symbol. We might see a shadow of what is going to be the next election’s coalition, like a preview, more or less,” he said.
Another Umno member at the assembly offered a similar reading, saying PAS’s attendance did not itself carry a formal political message as long as no such position had been announced by the top leadership.
PAS Youth delegates are seen seated in the front row at the 2026 Umno Youth General Assembly at the World Trade Centre in Kuala Lumpur, September 10, 2026. — Picture by Yusof Isa
But he said the exchange of delegations nevertheless showed that both parties were serious about the broader agenda of Malay-Muslim unity.
“Umno sent representatives to the
muktamar
, PAS sent representatives to PAU. That shows how serious both parties are about uniting the
ummah
,” he said.
Junaidi Ifdam Jun, 32, from Umno’s Batu Sapi division in Sabah, was more direct in his interpretation.
“For me, it means we will be together. That is what I feel,” he said.
The speculation is taking place against a backdrop that has changed considerably for Umno in recent months.
The party entered this year’s assembly buoyed by victories in Johor and Negri Sembilan.
BN won 48 of Johor’s 56 state seats, including 36 for Umno, while in Negeri Sembilan it secured 18 of 36 seats, with Umno winning all 16 seats it contested. Perikatan Nasional, led by PAS, secured seven.
PAS Muslimat delegates dressed in green sit in the front row among Umno members during the joint opening of the party’s Women, Youth and Puteri wing assemblies at the World Trade Centre in Kuala Lumpur, September 9, 2026. — Picture by Yusof Isa
The two coalitions subsequently agreed to work together to form the state administration.
Those results have given Umno delegates a renewed sense of confidence, while also raising the question of how far that momentum can be carried into the next contest.
Melaka is now the obvious test.
The state assembly’s term ends in December, and discussions over possible cooperation for the election are already underway.
Zahid has said negotiations would take place after the assembly is dissolved, while Dr Akmal has been more openly supportive of working with PAS in the state.
Dr Akmal has described Melaka as a test of whether “
penyatuan ummah
” can move beyond rhetoric and become an electoral strategy, pointing to the recent results in Johor and Negeri Sembilan as evidence of what cooperation can achieve.
That makes the PAS delegation’s appearance at the Umno assembly difficult to separate from the electoral calculations ahead, even if no formal pact has been announced.
For delegates like Ainnul, the immediate message is more about keeping the door open.
The exchanges between Umno and PAS have become more visible at a time when both parties are assessing what their next electoral moves could look like.

Title: Court rejects police bid to extend Abdul Azeez’s remand, former TH chairman set for release
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Former Tabung Haji (TH) chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim is expected to be released this evening after his remand period was not extended, said his lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad.
He said the police’s application to extend Abdul Azeez’s remand period for another three days to assist in the investigation under Section 420 of the Penal Code had been rejected, and the former Baling Member of Parliament is expected to be released before 5pm this evening once the previous remand period expires.
“Our side has strongly objected to the remand extension application on the grounds that our client is always ready and provides full cooperation to the police at any time if needed.
“The investigation can still continue without the need to remand our client. If the authorities require further evidence, he is ready to appear at Bukit Aman at any time,” he said when met by reporters outside the Dang Wangi district police headquarters (IPD) here today.
Abdul Azeez and two former TH officers were previously remanded for two days to assist in the investigation into a fraud case related to TH hibah.
Commenting on the lockup clothes and handcuffs he wore when he was arraigned on charges related to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) case yesterday, Amer Hamzah said Abdul Azeez was at that time under police custody for the remand proceedings.
“Our client only followed the instructions and SOPs set by the police. Therefore, there was no issue of any choice of clothing because he was being remanded by PDRM at the time,” he said.
Amer Hamzah said Abdul Azeez had appeared to give statements more than 10 times before and would continue to fully cooperate with the authorities to assist in the investigation. — Bernama

Title: Heavy rain, strong winds expected across KL, Putrajaya and seven states until 6pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and seven states until 6pm today.
It said in a statement that the adverse weather is forecast to affect Kuala Muda, Baling, Sik, Yan and Langkawi in Kedah; Timur Laut, Barat Daya, Seberang Perai Utara and Seberang Perai Tengah in Penang; and Kuala Pilah, Seremban, Jempol and Jelebu in Negeri Sembilan.
Similar weather conditions are also forecast in Larut Matang, Selama, Bagan Datuk, Manjung, Perak Tengah, Hilir Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Hulu Perak, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang and Muallim in Perak; Sepang, Petaling, Hulu Langat, Gombak, Klang and Kuala Langat in Selangor, as well as Cameron Highlands, Raub, Bentong, Bera, Jerantut and Lipis in Pahang.
In Sabah, the affected areas are the Interior (Sipitang, Tenom, Keningau, Tambunan, Membakut, Beaufort and Sook), West Coast, Tawau (Kunak and Lahad Datu), Sandakan (Kinabatangan) and Kudat (Kota Marudu). — Bernama

Title: Sarawak Flying Doctor Service operations suspended after fatal helicopter crash, says health minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — All Flying Doctor Service (FDS) operations in Sarawak have been temporarily suspended following a helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Miri, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said today.
In a statement, he said the suspension would allow the relevant authorities to investigate the incident and review existing safety and operational procedures.
“Emergency medical evacuation services for urgent cases will continue through cooperation between the Health Ministry and the Fire and Rescue Department,” he said.
Dzulkefly said the ministry would also discuss the possible use of Armed Forces assets to transport patients requiring emergency treatment to suitable healthcare facilities.
The ministry will conduct a comprehensive assessment of the FDS in Sarawak, covering its contracts, governance, operational safety, coverage needs and the effectiveness of its current service model.
“However, the safety of personnel and patients remains the ministry’s priority, alongside ensuring the continued delivery of healthcare services to rural communities,” he said.
The ministry is also reviewing FDS locations and access methods, including safe and practical transport alternatives, and will provide further updates to the public.

Title: Digital Ministry seeks Budget 2027 incentives to cut cost of digital tools for small traders
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 10 — The Digital Ministry has proposed incentives under Budget 2027 to make digital tools more affordable and encourage their adoption among small traders, Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said today.
He said the proposals were presented during a meeting with Finance Ministry officials two weeks ago as part of the government’s Budget engagement process.
“Our proposals largely focus on ensuring that technology capable of helping small traders does not merely exist, but is widely used so that its benefits can be felt,” he told reporters after the launch of a photography and art exhibition, Scars of War, at the Lin Xiang Xiong Art Gallery here.
“The government may need to consider providing incentives to reduce the cost of these tools and related expenses,” he added.
Gobind said the priority was to increase technology adoption and ensure it delivered a tangible impact to businesses and others who needed it.
“I have submitted many proposals, but it is better not to give the details one by one,” he said.
“Let the Finance Ministry make its decision and the prime minister announce it during or before the Budget,” he said.
Budget 2027 is scheduled to be tabled in Parliament on October 9.

Title: Hannah Yeoh confirms Pardons Board meeting as speculation over Najib’s bid mounts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh has confirmed that the Federal Territories Pardons Board (FTPB) will convene tomorrow morning.
Yeoh, who sits on the board as part of her portfolio, declined to disclose details regarding the agenda,
FMT
reported.
“Yes, I can confirm that tomorrow at 8.30am, there will be a pardons board meeting.
“We have been called, and that is all I can comment on for now,” she told reporters after an event today.
FMT
previously reported that former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s application is expected to be among the primary matters tabled before the board during this week's sitting.
It remains unclear whether the board will arrive at an immediate decision or limit the session to preliminary deliberations.
A separate source indicated that the possibility of allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his prison term under house arrest may be broached, though it is uncertain whether that option will be formally deliberated during the morning meeting.
Earlier today, Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said he was hoping for the “best” outcome tomorrow for Najib’s latest application.
Najib, 72, was convicted of misappropriating RM42 million belonging to SRC International and sentenced to 12 years in prison, along with a RM210 million fine. He began serving his sentence at Kajang Prison on Aug 23, 2022.
In 2024, the FT Pardons Board halved his prison term to six years and reduced the fine to RM50 million.
However, Najib and his lawyers subsequently insisted that the partial pardon came with a royal addendum for him to serve out his remaining time at home, eventually suing to have this granted.
On Dec 22 last year, High Court judge Alice Loke dismissed Najib’s application to serve the remainder of his reduced sentence under house arrest. Najib withdrew his appeal against the decision in April this year.

Title: Puteri Umno wishes Najib well ahead of expected clemency bid discussion
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Umno’s women’s youth wing, Puteri Umno, today extended its best wishes for former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s clemency bid ahead of a meeting expected to discuss his application.
This follows a report by
Free Malaysia Today
that the Federal Territories Pardons Board is expected to discuss Najib’s clemency application during its meeting this week.
Puteri Umno chief Datuk Nurul Amal Mohd Fauzi expressed the wing’s positive wishes during a press conference at the Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur (WTCKL) today.
“We hope all the best (for Najib).
“And we always prayed for the eased of everything,” Amal said.
Amal met local media after delivering her keynote address at the Puteri Umno General Assembly at WTCKL.
FMT had also previously reported that Najib’s application was expected to be among the issues raised at the board’s meeting, although it remained unclear whether the meeting would result in a decision or merely a discussion.
It also reported that Najib could potentially be allowed to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest, although it was unclear whether the option would be considered at the meeting.
Najib, 72, was convicted of misappropriating RM42 million belonging to SRC International and sentenced to 12 years in prison, along with a RM210 million fine.
He began serving his sentence at Kajang Prison on Aug 23, 2022.
The Pardons Board subsequently halved his prison term to six years and reduced the fine to RM50 million.
On Dec 22 last year, High Court judge Alice Loke dismissed Najib’s application to serve the remainder of his reduced sentence under house arrest. Najib later withdrew his appeal against the decision.

Title: Zahid to meet Negeri Sembilan MB over statement on proclamation involving Tuanku Muhriz
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said today he will meet Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim during the party’s general assembly to seek an explanation over his statement regarding a proclamation involving the state’s ruler.
Zahid said Ismail would meet him during the assembly, which began yesterday, although he did not specify when the meeting would take place.
“Yes, he will certainly meet me during this general assembly, and he will give an explanation. I will ask him about the background to his statement,” Zahid told reporters at the media centre here.
Asked when the meeting would take place, Zahid said: “The general assembly has already begun. I can give him a time to meet at any time.”
Ismail had reportedly said he signed a proclamation concerning the state’s ruler, Tuanku Muhriz Almarhum Tuanku Munawir, under duress.
He subsequently lodged a police report over the matter.
Zahid had yesterday denied reports that Aminuddin had resigned as menteri besar amid the dispute, saying the state government remained intact.

Title: Umno president Zahid says being optimistic about Najib’s pardon chances tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today said he was hoping for the best when the Pardons Board considers former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s clemency bid tomorrow.
Zahid reiterated today that the power of the pardon was constitutionally vested in the Yang diPertuan Agong.
“I am confident that His Majesty’s discretion and wisdom will determine the final decision, which is His Majesty’s absolute prerogative to announce,” he told reporters at the Umno general assembly here.
The Federal Territories Pardons Board is expected to discuss Najib’s latest application for tomorrow.
FMT reported that sources familiar with the matter said Najib’s application was expected to be among the issues raised at the board’s meeting, although it remained unclear whether the meeting would result in a decision or merely a discussion.
A separate source told the online news portal that Najib could potentially be allowed to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest, although it was unclear whether the option would be considered at the meeting.
Najib, 72, was convicted of misappropriating RM42 million belonging to SRC International and sentenced to 12 years in prison, along with a RM210 million fine. He began serving his sentence at Kajang Prison on Aug 23, 2022.
In 2024, the Pardons Board halved his prison term to six years and reduced the fine to RM50 million.
However, Najib and his lawyers subsequently insisted that the partial pardon came with a royal addendum for him to serve out his remaining time at home, eventually suing to have this granted.
On Dec 22 last year, High Court judge Alice Loke dismissed Najib’s application to serve the remainder of his reduced sentence under house arrest. Najib withdrew his appeal against the decision in April this year.

Title: King presents appointment instruments to Court of Appeal, High Court judges
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, today presented instruments of appointment to two judges at Istana Negara.
The ceremony began with the presentation to Court of Appeal judge Alice Loke Yee Ching, followed by High Court judge Elaine Yap Chin Gaik.
Present were Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said, Chief Justice Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh, Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar, Court of Appeal President Datuk Seri Abu Bakar Jais, Chief Judge of Malaya Datuk Seri Hashim Hamzah and Chief Judge of Sabah and Sarawak Datuk Azizah Nawawi.
Loke, 64, was appointed Senior Federal Counsel in 2013, a position she held until 2018. She was appointed a judicial commissioner of the Shah Alam High Court on July 10, 2020.
She was elevated to Shah Alam High Court judge on Jan 17, 2023, before being appointed to the Kuala Lumpur High Court’s Special Powers Division on Aug 18, 2025.
As a Kuala Lumpur High Court judge, Loke handled Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak’s judicial review application over an alleged addendum order allowing the former prime minister to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
During her tenure as Senior Federal Counsel, Loke was involved in several high-profile cases, including admiralty proceedings at the Kuala Lumpur High Court to seize the Equanimity, a vessel allegedly built using funds from 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB).
She also handled the Sulu claim and lawsuits filed against the Malaysian government over the disappearance of Malaysia Airlines flight MH370.
Meanwhile, Yap, 53, holds a Bachelor of Laws from the University of Sydney and a Diploma in International Arbitration from the Chartered Institute of Arbitrators.
She was appointed a judicial commissioner of the Shah Alam High Court on Aug 28, 2024, before taking up the same position at the Kuala Lumpur High Court on Nov 3, 2025. — Bernama

Title: Perak Assembly approves PKR chairman Mohamad Hairul as senator with 33 votes
Article:
IPOH, September 10 — The Perak Legislative Assembly today approved the appointment of Perak PKR chairman Mohamad Hairul Amir Sabri as a senator after he secured 33 votes in a secret ballot.
The 38-year-old defeated Perak PAS Dewan Ulama chairman Muhammad Zulkifli Muhammad Zakaria, the Opposition coalition’s candidate, who received 26 votes.
The election was held following the expiry of former senator and Perak Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Mujahid Yusuf Rawa’s term on May 24.
A total of 59 votes were cast by members of the Legislative Assembly.
The motion for the appointment was tabled by Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad and supported by Teja assemblyman Sandrea Ng Shy Ching (PKR).
Mohamad Hairul’s nomination was proposed by Ng and seconded by Lintang assemblyman Datuk Mohd Zolkfaly Haron (BN).
A Perak native, Mohamad Hairul holds a degree in Political Science from Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM).
He currently serves as chief special officer at the Office of Tambun MP, a position held by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
His previous appointments include serving on the Perak Water Board and as a non-executive and independent committee member of Panel International Bhd.
Mohamad Hairul has also served as Perak PKR chairman since 2024.

Title: Transboundary haze discussed on sidelines of Asean health ministers meeting, says Dzulkefly
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — The transboundary haze issue is not on the formal agenda of the 17th ASEAN Health Ministers Meeting (AHMM) and Related Meetings, but it is being discussed on the sidelines among health ministers of member states.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the matter could subsequently be taken up at the senior officers’ meeting.
“…we (will) do a side discussion among our ministers. That one we will continue to discuss. But perhaps, in our subsequent meeting, the senior officers’ meeting can carry this through. But as an agenda, unfortunately we are not there,” he said in a press conference after the launch of ASHA 2026-2030 here today.
However, Dzulkefly said the issue could be addressed within the scope of the existing health clusters.
When asked whether Malaysia planned to hold bilateral discussions with Indonesia on the haze issue, the health minister said: “We raised it, but we must follow through again.”
Yesterday, Communications Minister and Madani Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Malaysia is still awaiting confirmation from the Indonesian authorities before deploying assets that can be used to help tackle forest fires in the country, which had caused transboundary haze. — Bernama

Title: Dr Akmal: Umno Youth ready to work with PAS in Melaka, state is next test for Malay-Muslim unity
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Umno Youth is ready to work with PAS in the coming Melaka state election and believes its support among young voters can help deliver another electoral victory, Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh said today.
Dr Akmal, who is also the Merlimau assemblyman, described Melaka as a crucial test of whether “penyatuan ummah” — the idea of uniting Malay-Muslim political parties — could be translated from political rhetoric into an actual electoral strategy.
“Melaka isn’t just a state, it’s a test — to see if we can change the reality, and penyatuan becomes a basis and not just an idea.
“Johor has decided and Negri Sembilan has decided. So I ask Datuk Seri (Zahid), Melaka should be blue as well,” he said during his speech at the Umno Youth general assembly.He said Umno Youth was prepared to repeat the strong performance it recorded among young voters in the Johor and Negri Sembilan state elections.
Dr Akmal said the wing was prepared to cooperate with PAS in Melaka, while making clear that he was not seeking candidacy for himself.
“If we work with PAS in Melaka, Datuk Seri, I repeat, at this stage as the leader of Umno Youth I do not want to become a candidate if PH is a candidate there.
“However I believe you are smart, and I’m sure you don’t want to see the Umno Youth chief not compete. We will be there with you,” he said, referring to Umno president and BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi
Dr Akmals’ remarks come amid continuing discussions within Umno and BN over possible cooperation for the Melaka election.
Zahid said earlier this month that he had given Melaka Chief Minister and state BN chief Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh the mandate to negotiate cooperation with any party, with the eventual partner expected to be one that could help BN retain control of the state.
Zahid has also said formal negotiations would take place after the Melaka state assembly is dissolved, meaning no final electoral pact had been announced at the time of Dr Akmal’s speech.
Dr Akmal’s position was more specific, however, with the Umno Youth chief openly arguing for cooperation with PAS and presenting Melaka as the next opportunity to test the strategy after Johor and Negri Sembilan.
He said the wing also wanted the party to address issues affecting young Malaysians, including housing, childcare and the financial pressures faced by young families.
Dr Akmal’s Melaka pitch therefore combined a call for cooperation with PAS with a broader demand that Umno’s youth wing be given a meaningful role in shaping the party’s election platform.
The Melaka state assembly’s current term ends in December, while BN won 21 of the 28 seats in the 2021 state election, compared with five won by Pakatan Harapan and two by Perikatan Nasional.
During today’s assembly, Dr Akmal gave a particularly warm welcome to PAS Youth chief Afnan Hamimi Taib, describing the latter’s attendance as the culmination of three years of discussions between the two youth wings on national issues.
He said their pursuit of Malay-Muslim political unity predated the recent Johor and Negri Sembilan elections, where cooperation between Umno and PAS had already produced results.

Title: Malaysia’s unsold completed homes rise 8.6pc in H1 2026, but market is resilient, says Finance Minister II
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — More completed homes and serviced apartments were left unsold in the first half of 2026 compared with the preceding six months, according to the Property Market Report for the First Half of 2026.
The report, released by the Valuation and Property Services Department (JPPH) today, showed that the number of unsold completed homes rose by 8.6 per cent, from 30,471 units in the second half of 2025 to 33,094 units in the first half of 2026.
Their combined value increased slightly from RM17.73 billion to RM17.78 billion.
Despite the rise in unsold properties, Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said the overall property market remained resilient, recording 187,320 transactions worth RM105.12 billion between January and June 2026.
Residential properties accounted for 59.3 per cent of all transactions, with 110,998 deals recorded, and contributed 44.8 per cent of the total transaction value, or RM47.11 billion.
“Although there were some marginal adjustments, the property market remain steady due to stable price movements and transaction activities as well as active construction activities.
“The stability is also influenced by the country’s monetary policy that maintained the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) at 2.75 per cent, injecting confidence to both financiers and buyers,” he said before launching the report at the National Valuation Institute (Inspen) in Kajang, Selangor, today.
High-rise properties made up the largest portion of the unsold homes at 43.4 per cent, followed by terraced houses at 34.9 per cent.
About 37.3 per cent were priced at RM300,000 and below, while 38 per cent had been launched between six and 10 years ago.
Serviced apartments, which are classified separately under commercial properties, recorded a sharper increase of 24.7 per cent, from 18,752 unsold units worth RM15.42 billion in the second half of 2025 to 23,375 units worth RM19.33 billion in the first half of 2026.
More than half of the unsold serviced apartments, or 55.2 per cent, were priced between RM500,001 and RM1 million, while 71.1 per cent had been launched between six and 10 years ago.
Johor had the most unsold completed homes and serviced apartments, with 4,222 and 9,946 units, respectively.
At the same time, Johor recorded 6,697 new residential launches, the second-highest number after Selangor’s 8,354 units, while Penang ranked third with 2,878 units.
Homes priced between RM500,001 and RM1 million formed the largest segment of new launches nationwide, accounting for 10,853 units, or 39 per cent of the total.

Title: Kangar Bersatu deputy chief, 90 branch chiefs leave party over loss of trust in leadership
Article:
KANGAR, Sept 10 — Kangar Bersatu division deputy chief Faisol Rahman, together with the division committee and 90 of its 99 branch chiefs, announced tonight that they are leaving the party with immediate effect.
Also announcing their departure were the division’s Armada, Srikandi and Srikandi Muda leadership lines, including Armada Kangar deputy chief Mohd Firdaus Ismail and all Armada committee members.
Speaking at a press conference in Kuala Perlis last night, Faisol, on behalf of the group, said the move, however, did not involve any Bersatu Members of Parliament or state assemblymen within the division’s committee.
“This decision was made after careful deliberation, taking into account current developments and the views of the grassroots, who have lost faith in the central leadership.
“Having spent so long building the party at the grassroots level, we feel that trust in the party’s leadership has been lost,” he said.
Faisol said certain matters concerning the party’s direction, organisational management and leadership approach were no longer aligned with their hopes and aspirations as leaders at the division and branch levels.
He said the strength of a political party begins with trust between its leadership and grassroots members, and when that trust erodes, it is time for them to take a clear stand.
In light of this, he said they would be joining Parti Wawasan Negara, which is led by Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin.
Meanwhile, Perlis Bersatu leadership body chief Izizam Ibrahim said he viewed the resignations and departures positively, as it would enable an effective cleansing to strengthen the party in the state.
Izizam said that under Bersatu’s constitution, any resignation or vacancy within a division does not dissolve the division. Instead, a new organising committee will be formed to restructure the division’s leadership. — Bernama

Title: MOH still awaiting official post-mortem report on five Long Lellang crash victims
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is still awaiting the official report on the post-mortem findings of the five victims who were killed in the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, Sarawak.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the ministry was still awaiting official confirmation on the matter before providing further details to the public.
“As soon as we get everything officially, Datuk DG (Health director-general) will provide an explanation.
“Although we have heard about it, we have yet to receive anything official,” he told reporters at a press conference after the opening ceremony of the 17th Asean Health Ministers’ Meeting (AHMM) here today.
Also present were MOH secretary-general Datuk Seri Hasnol Zam Zam Ahmad and Health director-general Datuk Dr Mahathar Abdul Wahab.
Meanwhile, Dr Mahathar said the Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah had explained the procedures and processes related to the post-mortems in a statement yesterday, but the ministry was still awaiting a further announcement on the matter.
Yesterday, Mohamad Zainal confirmed that the five bodies of the victims killed in the helicopter crash had been successfully recovered from the crash site and flown from Long Lellang to Miri for post-mortems and related procedures. — Bernama

Title: Dismissing royal pardon powers undermines Federal Constitution, says Puteri Umno chief
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Puteri Umno chief Datuk Nurul Amal Mohd Fauzi today said that challenging or dismissing the royal power to grant pardons directly undermined the Federal Constitution.
During her keynote address at the Puteri Umno General Assembly, held in conjunction with the 2026 Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur, Amal described the royal institution as a key pillar of national sovereignty.
“Article 42 of the Federal Constitution grants the power of pardon to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, State Rulers, and Governors — challenging or dismissing this power directly undermines the Constitution itself.
“Respecting the Royal Institution and upholding the Constitution transcends partisan politics.
“Governments and political tides change, but the authority of the Monarchy and the Constitution must remain protected,” Amal said.
She added that political differences or interests were not a licence to erode the authority of the royal institution.
Also present were Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki, information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said and vice-president Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani.
The assembly was also attended by delegates from Singapore, Japan and the United Kingdom, as well as representatives of Ameerah Malaysia, PAS’ young women’s wing.
Puteri Umno is also marking its 25th anniversary at this year’s assembly.

Title: Nurse killed in helicopter crash had planned to leave flying doctor service to further studies
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 10 — The dream of nurse Jessie Paya Jok, 44, to further her studies was cut short when she was killed in the flying doctor service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang last Tuesday.
Her close friend, Caroline Sawai Joseph Chungat, 43, a nurse at Miri Hospital, said Jessie, or more fondly known as Paya, had told her that this month would be her last assignment with the FDS.
“That was the last conversation between Paya and me last month. She excitedly told me that this month would be her last assignment with the FDS as she was planning to pursue an Advanced Diploma in Midwifery next year.
“However, Paya’s aspiration and dream to further her studies did not materialise,” she said when contacted by Bernama.
Caroline said she had known Paya since 2005, when they were both community nurse trainees at the Ministry of Health Malaysia Training Institute (ILKKM) in Serian.
Throughout their 21-year friendship, Paya was described as a soft-spoken person who did not talk much, but always brightened the atmosphere around her with her smiles and laughter.
“Paya’s gentle nature was remarkable because throughout the more than two decades I knew her, I never once saw her lose her temper or raise her voice at anyone.”
“Paya’s kindness and sacrifices were also evident during her service at Bario Health Clinic, where her sincerity won the affection of the entire community in the remote area,” she said.
Caroline said Paya’s kindness was evident in her willingness to use her own money to cover the travel expenses of patients who needed to be referred to Miri Hospital for treatment.
“Not many people are capable of showing such compassion towards patients who are not related to them, but Paya demonstrated it through her dedication and her never-complaining attitude, even when faced with a workload that tested her mental and physical endurance,” she said.
Apart from Paya, Caroline also knew another nurse who was killed in the crash, Debra Moset, 40, who was known for her friendly, approachable nature and fondness for joking around.
“Our friendship began when we served together at Jambatan Suai Health Clinic for six years, before we were each transferred elsewhere and reunited in 2019 while undertaking the promotion by appointment (PSL) programme.
“Debra was meticulous and responsible in her duties. She was also known as a caring nurse among patients at Jambatan Suai Health Clinic,” she said.
Caroline added that her last conversation with Debra was in February and was solely about work.
Last Tuesday, the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) said a BO-105 helicopter carrying five people, including the pilot, crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport (STOLport).
Apart from Jessie and Debra, the other victims were pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30, medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33, and medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry, 31. — Bernama

Title: Digital minister says Malaysia’s draft AI Governance Bill complete, hopes to table it by Q1 2027
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 10 — Malaysia’s draft Artificial Intelligence (AI) Governance Bill has been completed and will be submitted to the Cabinet, Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said today.
He said the government was now setting up the structure needed to enforce the proposed law.
“We are hoping to table it this quarter or in the first quarter of next year,” he told reporters after launching the
Scars of War
photography and art exhibition at the Lin Xiang Xiong Art Gallery here.
The development marks the Bill’s progression beyond the drafting and public consultation stages reported earlier this year.
Gobind said the government must establish the agencies and administrative structure needed to monitor compliance and enforce the law before it takes effect.
“When we enforce a law, we must ensure there are parties that can make certain the law is complied with,” he said.
“If it is not complied with, action must be taken. That particular structure has to be set up,” he explained.
“We are looking at how to establish a structure to ensure that once the Bill is passed, there will already be parties responsible for ensuring compliance, investigating problems and enforcing the law,” he said.
Gobind said the proposed legislation would form part of a broader AI governance framework combining technical standards, regulations and laws.
“When we look at the AI governance process, it is broader than a Bill. It involves three things — standards, regulations and laws,” he said.
He said standards could address matters involving technology developers and users, while regulations would cover issues requiring closer oversight but not specific legislation.
“There are aspects that require more attention but do not reach the stage where a law is needed. In those circumstances, we look at regulations,” he said.
Gobind said regulations would allow the government to respond more quickly as AI technology evolved and new challenges emerged.
“This will be more effective because we are looking at a world where issues will arise quickly due to the nature of the technology,” he said.
He said matters requiring specific legal provisions would be addressed through the Bill, which must be tabled in Parliament.
Gobind added that AI Malaysia had been established as part of preparations for the wider governance framework, while a standards centre set up last month had begun working with SIRIM and other organisations.

Title: Alam Maritim CEO charged with fraud over vessel charter rates, claims trial
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Alam Maritim Resources Bhd group managing director and chief executive officer (CEO) Datuk Azmi Ahmad was charged in the Sessions Court here today on two charges of fraud relating to the daily charter rate of a vessel.
Azmi, 67, however, pleaded not guilty after both charges were read out before Judge Suzana Hussin.
“Understand (the charges), I plead not guilty and request to be tried,” he said after the charges against him were read out one by one.
According to the first charge, Azmi is charged with defrauding TH Alam Management Sdn Bhd principal officer Iskandar Mohd Zaffa, 48, by concealing the actual offer of Daily Charter Rate dated August 24, 2023 which allocated RM80,500 per day in the Work Order.
The act allegedly prompted Iskandar to agree to sign the BIMCO Supplytime 2017 with a Daily Charter Rate of RM70,000 per day between Alam-JV DP2 (L) Inc. and Alam Maritim (M) Sdn Bhd.
For the second charge, he is charged with defrauding the same individual by concealing the actual Daily Charter Rate offer dated 15 Jan 2024 which allocated a total of RM110,000 per day in the Work Order, thus prompting the man to sign BIMCO Supplytime 2017 with a Daily Charter Rate, RM78,000 per day between TH-Alam Management and Alam Maritim.
The offence was allegedly committed at a building in Jalan Radin Anum, Bandar Baru Sri Petaling here on Sept 6 2023 and Jan 16 2024, under Section 417 of the Penal Code (Act 574) which provides for a maximum imprisonment of five years or a fine or both, if convicted.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Noor Syazwani Mohammad Sobry offered bail of RM500,000 with one surety, with additional conditions that the accused must report to the Putrajaya MACC office every three months and is prohibited from interfering with prosecution witnesses until the case is resolved.
However, lawyer Wan Muhd Ariff Ameer Wan Normazlan, who represented Azmi, requested that the bail be reduced to RM100,000 because the amount offered was too high and that his client had cooperated well throughout the investigation.
“The purpose of the bail is to ensure that my client attends court. My client has a wife and six children, the youngest of whom is six years old, and the accused also has health problems that require examination,” he said.
Wan Muhd Ariff Ameer also requested that the passport taken by the MACC be returned to the accused because his client is not at risk of fleeing.
Suzana then allowed the accused to be granted bail of RM300,000 with one surety, with additional conditions as requested by the prosecution.
The court has set Nov 18 for mention of the case for submission of documents. — Bernama

Title: No hazardous API readings recorded nationwide, Sarawak records highest unhealthy levels
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — No areas recorded hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) readings due to haze as of 9 am today.
According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, eight areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy readings, namely Sarikei (194), Serian district police headquarters (IPD) (183), Samarahan (180), Kuching (171), Samalaju (164), Sri Aman (157), Sibu (155) and Mukah (154).
Meanwhile, four areas in Johor also recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Larkin (140), Kluang (125), Batu Pahat (115) and Pasir Gudang (114).
In Kuala Lumpur, Batu Muda also recorded an unhealthy API reading of 167.
Overall, 48 areas nationwide were reported to be at the moderate level, while seven areas recorded good air quality readings.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 (moderate), 101 to 200 (unhealthy), 201 to 300 (very unhealthy) and 301 and above (hazardous). — Bernama

Title: ‘Flabbergasted’: Lawyer says lock-up attire, handcuffs were not former TH chairman Abdul Azeez’s choice
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim’s lawyer has rejected the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission’s (MACC) assertion that his client chose to appear in court wearing a purple lock-up shirt and handcuffs yesterday.
In a statement, Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad said police instructed Azeez to change from his normal clothes into purple lock-up attire and handcuffed him before taking him to court for a remand hearing.
After a two-day remand order was granted, Amer said Azeez was taken directly to another courtroom for the MACC charge to be read without being given an opportunity to change.
“At all material times, our client remained under the custody and control of the police. The handcuffs placed on him were also by the police and not by the MACC,” he said.
“Accordingly, our client’s appearance in the purple lock-up attire and handcuffs during the subsequent MACC proceedings was not a matter of his personal choice,” he added.
Amer said he was “flabbergasted” by the MACC’s account, adding that Azeez reserved the right to take legal action against anyone who published what he described as a false or misleading version of events.
Azeez yesterday pleaded not guilty to using his position to influence TH’s decision to invest RM190 million in Putrajaya Perdana Bhd, a company in which he was alleged to have an interest, and was granted bail of RM450,000.
Separately, he was remanded for two days until tomorrow following an application by Bukit Aman’s Commercial Crime Investigation Department, with reports suggesting he is being investigated under anti-money laundering laws.

Title: ‘No need to erase history’: Wanita Umno defends Najib’s legacy amid ‘legal process’
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — The women’s wing of Umno has reaffirmed its loyalty to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, asserting that the party does not need to “erase history” to build its future.
Speaking at the Wanita Umno general assembly today, the wing’s chief, Datuk Seri Noraini Ahmad, urged the party to appreciate leaders who devoted their lives to the service of Umno and the nation.
“We appreciate those who have contributed to the party. We appreciate the leaders of the past who devoted a large part of their lives to Umno and the country.
“And Wanita Umno also does not forget the contributions of Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak. We do not need to erase history to build the future,” Noraini said in her policy speech.
Noraini, who also serves as the Minister of plantation and commodities, argued that Najib’s impact on the country’s economic transformation, infrastructure development, and public assistance remains an undeniable part of Malaysia’s history, regardless of the current political climate.
While acknowledging the ongoing legal proceedings involving the former prime minister, she maintained that respect for the judiciary does not preclude the expression of human compassion.
“But respecting the legal process does not prevent us from having human values. Wanita Umno knows how to remember the contributions of others,” she said.
Concluding her address, Noraini offered prayers for Najib and his family, expressing hope that they would find the strength and resilience to endure their current trials.
“We continue to pray that the doors of justice and compassion will be opened, so that he can return to his family and continue the struggle together,” she said.
Najib is currently serving a prison sentence from one of his convictions over the 1MDB global corruption scandal.

Title: Ceiling fire at Jengka Hospital wards forces 17 to evacuate, no injuries reported
Article:
KUANTAN, Sept 10 — Part of the ceiling in the paediatric and women’s wards at Jengka Hospital caught fire last night, but all 17 individuals in the wards escaped unhurt.
Maran district police chief Supt Wong Kim Wai said police were alerted to the incident at about 7 pm.
He said the fire involved the ceiling space of both wards and was fully extinguished by the Pahang Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) in about 20 minutes.
“Six boys, five girls, and six women who were in the wards managed to escape safely, and none sustained injuries,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Wong said initial information from Pahang JBPM indicated that the fire originated above the ceiling of the two wards, causing about 10 per cent damage to the wiring and ceiling structure.
He added that the cause of the fire and the estimated losses were still under investigation. — Bernama

Title: Man killed by elephant while searching for missing cow in Kuala Krai
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Sept 10 — A 66-year-old man was believed to have been killed by an elephant while searching for his missing cow at the Lepan Kabu plantation in Kuala Krai this afternoon.
Kuala Krai police chief Supt Mazlan Mamat said that following a report at 4 pm, a joint team of police, Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan), and Civil Defence Force was deployed to the scene.
“The team secured the area before recovering the victim’s remains,” he told Bernama yesterday.
Meanwhile, Pahi Mukim chief Mohd Khairul Anuar Mohd Nor identified the victim as Ghazali Setapa, from Kampung Pahi.
Mohd Khairul Anuar said Ghazali had gone to the plantation with his two sons and three friends to look for his missing cow. The group had then split up. One of them had spotted an elephant and a member of the group was sent to notify Perhilitan.
Moments later, they claimed to have heard trumpeting nearby, followed the sound, and discovered the victim, apparently killed by the animal.
Mohd Khairul Anuar said the victim’s body was sent to Hospital Sultan Ismail Petra’s Forensic Unit for a post-mortem.
He added that while elephants had strayed into the area before, the last such incident was two to three years ago, and this animal is believed to have lost its way as the area is not their natural habitat. — Bernama

Title: Man dies after suspected heart attack, falls into septic tank pit in Kota Bharu
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Sept 10 — A man died after he is believed to have suffered a heart attack and fallen into a three-metre-deep septic tank pit under construction in Taman Permai, Demit, near here yesterday afternoon.
Kota Bharu Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) chief Mohd Ridwan Baharuddin said the department received an emergency call at 5.28 pm. Firefighters arrived at the scene at 5.37 pm and found a man lying unconscious inside a three-metre-deep hole.
Firefighters extricated the victim using a stretcher before Ministry of Health medical personnel examined him, he said last night.
The victim, Zakari Mat Jusoh, 48, was confirmed dead at the scene by medical officers.
He added that family members reported the victim had a history of heart problems and a medical appointment last week.
“At the time of the incident, the victim was reportedly measuring the hole to install a septic tank when he collapsed and fell in. Initial assessments by the medical team suspect the victim suffered a heart attack before collapsing,” he said.
Mohd Ridwan said the operation ended at 5.53 pm and the body was handed over to the police for further action. — Bernama

Title: NRD: 365 foreigners charged over fake MyKad, birth certificate offences in eight months
Article:
PORT KLANG, Sept 10 — The National Registration Department (NRD) disclosed that 365 foreigners were charged in court over MyKad and birth certificate fraud between January and August this year.
Enforcement director Mazhad Abdul Aziz said 738 joint operations were conducted with various agencies nationwide, including raids on premises and factories to detect the use of fraudulent identification documents.
“Of that number, 286 cases involved the use of fake identity cards or cards belonging to others, while another 79 were linked to forged birth certificates.
“Most of those arrested were Indonesian and Filipino nationals,” he told reporters after leading Ops Layar at a printing factory in Bandar Sultan Suleiman here last night.
Mazhad added that the prosecutions were carried out under the National Registration Regulations 1990 and the Births and Deaths Registration Act 1957 (Act 299).
“We will continue to mount integrated and targeted enforcement operations to crack down on such activities,” he emphasised.
Meanwhile, he said Ops Layar, which ran for four hours starting at 5.00 pm, involved 52 NRD personnel from Putrajaya, Selangor and Kuala Lumpur, as well as 15 officers from the Malaysian Immigration Department in Putrajaya and the Selangor Department of Labour.
“A total of 195 individuals were inspected, including 63 locals who were found to possess valid identity cards.
“Three women, aged between 21 and 37, believed to be Indonesian nationals, were detained on suspicion of using counterfeit identity cards or cards belonging to others to secure employment at the factory,” he said. — Bernama
